Subject: Post-demo tech sync: private connectivity & embeddings/reranker routing

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the thoughtful questions. I promised a short recap and a recommended next-steps checklist for the integration path we discussed (SDK, auth, routing, embeddings + reranker). Notes below, followed by concrete action items.

Key design choices we discussed:
- Private connectivity: you indicated preference for a VPC Endpoint (private link) with mTLS between CoreSight and Redwood.
- Auth: short-lived tokens from your control plane + Azure AD backed service account for provisioning.
- Routing: route embedding and rerank calls to a dedicated model pool to keep latency predictable.
- Structured output/tool-calling: plan to surface structured JSON responses for downstream pipelines; tool calls will be gated behind allowlists.

Action items (proposed owners & ETA):
1) Confirm IP ranges and preferred egress posture (do you want full VPC peering or just endpoint + NAT?) — Andrew / Ops — reply by Tue 20 Apr
2) Send sample QPS and 95th latency SLA target for embeddings and reranker (helps sizing) — Andrew — reply by Tue 20 Apr
3) Share mTLS cert thumbprint and preferred cipher suite (we support modern TLS1.3 ciphers) — ops@coresight.ai — ASAP
4) Redwood to provide endpoint checklist + SDK snippet for mutual auth and structured output parsing — Grace / Marissa — EOD Mon 19 Apr

Attachments: I’ll attach a short VPC endpoint checklist and an SDK snippet in a follow-up (see attachment stub).

If helpful, we can book a 30-min engineering pairing session next week to walk through the VPC connector and a quick end-to-end embedding call.

Best,

Thanks Grace — quick replies inline and a couple questions.

Inline:
- IP ranges / egress: we prefer the VPC endpoint approach (private link). Our infra team will still route egress through a NAT for other services. I can confirm we can reserve two /28 blocks if needed.
- QPS / latency targets: baseline for embeddings is ~50 qps during steady-state, spikes to 150 qps. Target 95th latency for embeddings <120ms; reranker calls are lower QPS (~10 qps) but need <200ms 95th.
- mTLS: we can provision certs and would prefer mutual TLS + client cert rotation every 30 days.

Attachments: attaching a short ops note with our IP ranges and a placeholder for the cert chain (ops attached as coresight-mtls-keys.txt).

Questions:
1) For structured output: can Redwood guarantee stable JSON schema across model rollouts or do we need schema-anchoring in the app?
2) For tool-calling: we need allowlist controls per customer workspace — can we scope that to a specific API key and model route?

Happy to do the pairing session — Thu 22 Apr or Fri 23 Apr would work for our infra and security folks.

—Andrew

- For the Dedicated path, estimated monthly commit for your stated steady-state (50 qps embeddings + buffer) would be in the ballpark of $18k–$25k depending on retention/throughput. I can put together a formal quote after we confirm exact peak QPS and retention window for KV cache.

Thanks everyone — below is a concise engineering checklist and answers to Andrew's questions. I included code snippets as attachment stubs and a proposed agenda for the pairing session.

Short answers to questions:
- Stable JSON schema: Redwood does not silently change the structured output schema. We recommend schema-anchoring in the client (validate fields & versions) and we provide a version field in the response to detect model-side schema changes. For strict contracts we can gate model rollouts behind acceptance tests tied to your prompt set.
- Tool-calling allowlists: yes — allowlists are scoped to API keys and route configurations. We can restrict tool invocation to a specific model route and workspace-level key.

Engineering checklist (actions we will take / what we need from CoreSight):
1) VPC Endpoint & Networking
   - Redwood provides a VPC endpoint host and an expected set of IP ranges for our egress (attachment: redwood-vpc-endpoint-cheatsheet.pdf).
   - CoreSight provides the preferred subnet (/28 blocks) and whether you will NAT other traffic through the same peering. (Owner: CoreSight ops)
   - mTLS: exchange client CA bundle; we support cert rotation via a short-lived client cert process. (Owner: CoreSight ops)

2) SDK & Auth
   - Use Redwood SDK (we'll provide snippet) with mTLS handshake + short-lived token refresh flow. Example flow in attachment: sdk-mtls-snippet.txt.
   - For server-to-server flows use Azure AD service principal to mint tokens into your control plane, then exchange for Redwood session tokens via our auth callback.

3) Routing & Model Pools
   - Create a dedicated model route for embeddings + reranker; route is pinned to a dedicated pool to reduce tail latency. We'll configure autoscaling thresholds based on the QPS profile you provided.

4) Embeddings / Reranker sizing guidance
   - Baseline 50 qps steady -> recommend starting with 2 dedicated GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache configured for 24hr TTL. If you expect using large context windows often, notify us so we can adjust kernel selection and batch size.

5) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We'll attach a sample 'schema-anchored' prompt and a parsing helper in the SDK. Tool calls will be restricted by API key and explicit allowlist entries.

Pairing session agenda (60 min)
- 00:00–00:05 Intro / goals (Grace)
- 00:05–00:20 VPC endpoint walkthrough & cert exchange (Monica + CoreSight ops)
- 00:20–00:35 SDK demo: mTLS + token exchange + embedding call (Marissa)
- 00:35–00:50 Reranker sizing exercise + Q&A (Monica)
- 00:50–01:00 Next steps & action owners (Aditya)

Proposed times: Thu 22 Apr 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 23 Apr 09:00–10:00 PT. Please confirm which works best.

Attachments (stubs): redwood-vpc-endpoint-cheatsheet.pdf, sdk-mtls-snippet.txt, sample-schema-prompt.json

—Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
